subject: Post-call: Acme integration & model-routing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Acme integration & model-routing next steps

Hi Alex / Sophie,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of decisions:
- Integration approach: server-side Redwood SDK for backend calls (preferred) with short-lived bearer tokens.
- Auth: Acme prefers Okta/OIDC for service-to-service - we can support OIDC-based service accounts; will follow up with Marcus/Dev on token rotation details.
- Model routing & policies: primary routing to US regional fleet, latency SLO 200ms p95 for chat flows. Fallback chain to lower-cost/quantized variants when latency slack is available.
- Structured output & tool-calling: we'll use Redwood's structured output schema for invoicing/extraction flows and enable tool-calling hooks for internal APIs (we discussed the payments lookup example).
- Search: use embeddings + lightweight neural reranker for semantic results (embed queries in the US region and rerank on a smaller candidate set).

Action items (owners and ETA):
1) Redwood: share a sketched integration architecture + MAcP (attached) - Marissa - EOD 3/1 (attached).
2) Acme: confirm auth path (Okta OIDC vs. API key) and roster of infra people for technical deep-dive - Alex/Sophie - by 3/3.
3) Redwood infra: provide example SDK init and model-routing policy snippet, including recommended fallback chain - Dev - by 3/2.
4) Joint: schedule 60m technical deep-dive with infra/security/product - Marissa to propose slots.

Notes on recommended defaults (so your engineers have something to start with):
- SDK: server-side initialization with short-lived bearer tokens. Example snippet attached in follow-up email.
- Routing policy (high level): prefer region -> latency tier -> cost tier. For chat: p95 latency target 200ms, route to low-latency variant first, else fallback to cost-optimized quantized model (prefetch KV cache when possible).
- Embeddings: 512-d base model quantized for storage; reranker to run on top-8 candidates to keep cost down.

Attachments: redwood-architecture-sketch.png, acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue 3/8 9-10am PT, Wed 3/9 11am-12pm PT, Thu 3/10 2-3pm PT - can you confirm which works?

Thanks - happy to jump on a quick sync if you want to walk through the doc.

Best,

Alex / Sophie -

Short answers up front:
- Yes, Redwood supports OIDC-based service accounts for private deployments and for Dedicated customers; for hosted API we support token-exchange flows and can integrate with Okta via OIDC + a short-lived token broker. We can share our recommended flow docs and sample config.
- Reranker latency depends on model size; with a lightweight reranker (distil ranking model) you should expect ~15-240ms per candidate on GPU. If you rerank top-8 candidates, budget ~200-400ms depending on instance type and batch settings.

Example SDK init (pseudo):
// server-side init
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({
  auth: { type: 'oidc', tokenEndpoint: 'https://okta.acme.com/oauth2/v1/token', clientId: 'ACME-SVC', clientSecretRef: 'kms://acme/svc-secret' },
  region: 'us-west-2',
});

Routing policy (high level text):
- primary: route by region (us-west-2) 
- latency_policy: p95 <= 200ms for chat routes
- fallback_chain: ["redwood-chat-llama-16b-lowlat", "redwood-chat-gptx-8b-quant", "redwood-chat-gptx-8b-small"]
- cost_policy: when cost_threshold_exceeded then prefer quantized variants and increase batching for non-interactive flows

Notes on KV / caching: pre-warm KV cache for expected session tokens (helps p95); prefer per-customer prefix caching if you have multiplexed tenants.

Security notes: token rotation is recommended every 15m-60m for short-lived tokens; we can also support customer-managed KMS for signing if you want to avoid storing client secrets in Redwood.

Proposed attendees for deep-dive: Acme infra, Acme security, Acme product (Alex), Marcus (Redwood infra), Dev (Redwood infra), Marissa (AE).

Slots that work for us: Tue 3/8 9-10am PT (confirmed tentative), Wed 3/9 11am-12pm PT. I'll add a short agenda: 1) auth and network (20m) 2) routing & latency/cost policy (20m) 3) embeddings/reranker design (15m) 4) next steps / MAcP (5m).

Attaching a small architecture sketch and the mutual action plan again for visibility.

Thanks,
